acceptedAnswer.text: Divide your ad spend by your number of purchases over the same period. €1,000 spent for 40 purchases gives a €25 CPA. To know if it is profitable, compare it to your break-even CPA: average order value minus product cost, shipping and payment fees.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between CPA and CAC?

acceptedAnswer.text: CPA measures the ad cost of a purchase, whether it comes from a new customer or an existing one. CAC measures the cost of acquiring a new customer and often includes spending beyond ads. In ecommerce, CPA is used to run a campaign and CAC to judge how profitable a customer is over their lifetime.

It is the maximum cost per purchase before you lose money on an order. You get it by subtracting the product cost, shipping and payment fees from your average order value. At this CPA, the sale pays back the ad without earning anything.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between CPA and ROAS?

acceptedAnswer.text: CPA measures what a purchase costs, ROAS what each euro of ad spend brings back. The two are linked: ROAS = average order value / CPA. A CPA below your break-even CPA equals a ROAS above your BEROAS.

mainEntity.name: What is a good CPA in ecommerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: A CPA below your break-even CPA, with enough room to cover your fixed costs and your margin. There is no universal number: it depends on your average order value and your costs. Set a target net margin in the calculator to get your own target CPA.

mainEntity.name: Why does my CPA go up when I increase the budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bigger budget pushes the platform to reach people who are less likely to buy, and the same people see your ad more often. CPC goes up or conversion drops. Raise the budget step by step and check your CPA after each step.

mainEntity.name: Should I include shipping and payment fees?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They shrink what is left of each order to pay for ads. Forgetting a few euros of shipping or payment fees can make a campaign look profitable when it is losing money on every sale.
